manta.name: MANTA
manta.title: Manta
manta.headline:
Giant
manta rays
manta.lede:
Giant manta rays glide through the ocean,
filtering plankton from the water.
manta.story: Giant manta rays use broad, wing-like fins to move through tropical and subtropical seas. They filter plankton from the water.
manta.alt: A giant manta ray gliding through dark blue ocean water.

orca.name: ORCA
orca.title: Orca
orca.headline:
Life in
family groups
orca.lede:
Orcas use calls to communicate and echolocation to find prey.
Hunting traditions pass between generations.
orca.story: Orcas are highly social dolphins. They use calls to communicate and echolocation to find prey. Family groups pass hunting behaviours between generations.
orca.alt: A single orca swimming through deep, cold blue water.

medusa.name: MEDUSA
medusa.title: Medusa
medusa.headline:
How jellyfish
move
medusa.lede:
Jellyfish swim by pulsing their bells
and drift with the currents.
medusa.story: Jellyfish move by pulsing their bells and drifting with ocean currents. Some species produce their own light. Medusa is an artistic portrait of a jellyfish, not a depiction of an identified species.
medusa.alt: A translucent jellyfish with delicate trailing tentacles in the dark ocean.

description: Manta rays, orcas and jellyfish: see them in motion and learn how they feed, move and communicate.

gallery.intro: Open an image to view the portrait.

notes.title: How manta rays feed
notes.body: Manta rays filter plankton from seawater. The fins beside their mouths, called cephalic fins, help guide water in.
notes.source: Read about manta rays at NOAA

notes.title: Orca calls and hunting
notes.body: Orcas use calls to communicate and echolocation to explore their surroundings. Family groups pass behaviours between generations. Different populations can have different diets and ways of hunting.

notes.title: Why some ocean animals glow
notes.body: Bioluminescence is light produced by a chemical reaction. Some ocean animals use it to defend themselves, find food or communicate.
